subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `ChannelTtsVoiceDeliveryCapabilities.captionedFinalText` as the contract by which channel plugins opt into deferred final-TTS text delivery and fallback handling?
rationale: The implementation deliberately changes shared core-to-plugin delivery semantics and documentation; source review can assess consistency, but only owners can decide whether this should be a durable public channel capability.

options.title: Approve the generic capability
options.body: Keep the capability-based design, contingent on current-head Telegram proof that covers the deferred-text and fallback behavior.

options.title: Keep delivery policy channel-owned
options.body: Reject the new shared capability and redesign the behavior behind an existing Telegram-owned seam if maintainers do not want this SDK contract.

options.title: Pause for broader channel semantics
options.body: Defer the PR until maintainers define whether other caption-capable channels should share the same text-suppression contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic capability
recommendation.body: Keep the capability-based design, contingent on current-head Telegram proof that covers the deferred-text and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The recorded mention and subscription provide the strongest available evidence of responsibility for deciding whether this new shared delivery contract should exist.
